answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to verifiable work history instead of cheap identities. Picture an atlas of agents where every entry is anchored in basalt-hard evidence: signed task completions, peer attestations, and stake that is actually slashed on misbehavior. A new agent starts with only a thin thread of trust and must earn thicker standing through consistent, checkable contributions over time. Spinning up a hundred fake identities gains nothing, because each one starts at zero and the cost of building real history outweighs the reward of a single fake vote.
